results.name: AI-generated content policy for Market and Elements
results.title: AI-generated content policy for Market and Elements
results.body:
Summary: These guidelines set out rules around using content generated with third-party artificial intelligence tools such as DALL-E, Stable Diffusion and Midjourney.

The new field of AI-generated content poses some questions around legal rights and risks. This policy is aimed at achieving the fairest and safest result for both the author community and our customers.

Keep in mind that there are different rules for assets used in item previews (these assets are for preview purposes only, and don’t get distributed to your customers) and assets in the item download (refers to assets that are actually included in the download files).

Authors are not allowed to sell AI-generated content

You may not publish or submit AI-generated content, either as a standalone item or as the primary component of your item's final download file.

This is due to the legal concerns around AI-generated content. As per our Author Terms & Contributor Agreement, you are required to have the right necessary license items, and be able to warrant that the buyer's use of them does not infringe on the rights of others. As AI-generation models may be based on the intellectual property of many creators, this type of content does not meet our requirements.

What does that mean? This means that you cannot sell AI-generated content as the main component of your item. This extends to all content types, across Market and Elements.

  • As an example, you cannot use AI tools to generate an illustration, and submit it to the Illustration category on GraphicRiver or Elements.

AI-generated content is allowed for item Previews ONLY

AI-generated content can be used for preview purposes only, and must not be included in the download file.

Please note that just as with any other assets used within your item preview, it remains your responsibility to ensure that you have the correct commercial license to use the asset within the item preview. For more information, please see What assets can I use in my items?

  • As an example, you can use AI tools to generate an illustration and use it as a preview image in your blog template, provided the AI license allows you to do this. The image cannot be included in the download file.
  • If your item includes a demo content import, AI-generated content can be imported directly from your server, as long as it is not included in the item zip file.

Please note that as the field of AI-generated content is rapidly changing, these guidelines may also be updated with additional rules — watch this space for further updates.

results.name: Author applications are paused — new authors join by invitation only
results.title: Author applications are paused — new authors join by invitation only
results.body:
We're not accepting open applications from new authors. There's no application form to fill out, and no waitlist to join. Instead, we're inviting authors directly for a small number of categories where we need more work.

We know that's frustrating if you've been waiting to apply, and we're sorry for the inconvenience. Please check back for updates.

This means:

  • Envato Elements: not accepting new author sign-ups.
  • Envato Market: new author accounts can't be created at this time.
  • The only way to join right now is to be invited directly by Envato for a category we've identified as needing more work.

This article explains why, which categories are affected, and what you can do while open applications stay paused.

Why are open applications paused?

We’re improving how we review applications, refining our onboarding experience, and strengthening our overall category strategy across Envato Elements and Envato Market.

Pausing open applications while we redesign and moving to direct invitations helps ensure that when authors are selected for intake, we can support them with:

  • Clearer expectations
  • Better category alignment
  • Stronger opportunities for success

What does 'invitation-only' mean?

When we identify a category that needs more work, we reach out directly to creators we think are a strong fit. 

We no longer accept applications across all content types, focusing instead on a defined set of categories where customer demand is highest and where we can best support author success.

What can I do while open applications are paused?

While applications are paused, you can:

  • Explore the Author Hub to understand category trends and customer demand
  • Continue building and refining your best work
  • Prepare items that demonstrate originality, technical quality, and strong commercial relevance

Being ready ahead of time will help when applications reopen.

When will applications reopen?

We don't have a confirmed reopening date yet. When applications do reopen, the updated author application form will be available, along with guidance on eligible categories and submission requirements. 

FAQs

  • Are you still accepting applications from new authors?

    We're not accepting open applications. The only way to join as a new author right now is via our selective intake model for supported content types only.

  • Can I request an invitation, or apply to be considered?

    There's no form, waitlist, or process to request an invitation. Invitations are sent directly by Envato to creators we've identified for a specific category. Submitting work, following up, or reaching out to support won't move you into consideration.

  • Will all content categories be open when applications return?

    No. Only selected content categories will be supported when applications reopen. Requirements will vary by category, including platform availability and submission methods. These details will be shared when applications reopen.

  • What categories won’t be reopening?

    At this stage, we're not inviting authors into Theme, Code, Photo, Audio, or Graphics (with the exception of Animated Graphics and Fonts, which will open later in 2026). This is subject to change based on subscriber demand and content priorities.

  • If my content type isn't part of the current invitations, is that category being phased out?

    No. Not being part of the current intake doesn’t mean your category is being phased out or removed. We’ll continue to support and work with our existing pool of authors in those categories.

  • Will you notify me if invitations open up in my category?

    Will you notify me if invitations open up in my category? No, we won't be sending individual notifications. Keep an eye on this article for updates.

  • Can I create an account now and upload content later?

    No. While open applications are paused, you can't create a new Envato author account unless you've been invited.

  • I’m a Graphics author and want to upload LUTs. What should I do?

    LUTs sit within the Video category. Video isn't currently accepting open applications, so you'd need to be invited as a Video author.

  • Can existing authors apply to join another category during the pause?

    No. Existing authors can't apply to add new content types or categories while open applications are paused. This would require an invitation for that category, same as a new author.

  • Will you be accepting AI-generated content in the future?

    Not at this time. We're not currently inviting authors for AI-generated content. Any changes to this will be communicated through official Envato channels.
results.snippet: consideration. Will all content categories be open when applications return? No. Only selected content categories will be supported

results.name: Envato Elements subscription pricing tiers and author revenue share
results.title: Envato Elements subscription pricing tiers and author revenue share
results.body:
Summary: We're introducing new subscription pricing tiers for Envato Elements from 25 February 2026. This article explains what's changing and what this means for you.

What’s changing with Envato Elements pricing?

We’re introducing new subscription pricing tiers for Envato Elements from 25 February 2026. Customers will be able to choose from higher-tier plans that extend access to AI generations, while our existing base subscription plan will have limits.

Are customers paying more for the same stock content?

No. The base Envato Elements subscription continues to provide access to the same stock asset library as it does today. Higher-tier plans offer additional Gen AI generations on top of this existing content offering. 

Does this change how I am paid under subscriber share?

The Author share will continue to be calculated based on the base subscription price, just as it is today, including the 50/50 split for Individual and Teams subscriptions.

Does this affect how item points or usage are calculated?

No. Item usage, item points, and how revenue is distributed across authors based on content usage remain unchanged.

Why isn’t all subscription revenue shared with authors?

The incremental portion above the base subscription plan represents the fee for access to our GenAI offering and is used to fund the delivery and ongoing operation of GenAI functionality and our broader platform.

Are authors compensated when their content is used in a Gen AI tool?

Yes — authors earn when their content is used with eligible AI tools. 

For example, with tools like ImageEdit, a customer can select an image from our library and use the tool to modify or enhance it. In these cases, the original image is licensed as usual, and the author is paid through a standard license. 

To be clear: the use of this edit tool does not contribute to AI training or to improve AI models. Your item remains yours — and you’re compensated when it’s used.

What’s not changing?

  • The subscriber share model remains in place for shareable net revenue
  • Earnings distribution based on author content usage remains the same.
  • Base subscriptions continue to contribute to the author revenue pool as they do today.

results.title: Acceptable Use Policy
results.body:
Last revised: September 25, 2025

About this policy

  1. Hi, we're Envato and welcome to our Acceptable Use Policy. This policy applies to all Users of the Envato Sites and sets out what you can and cannot do with the Envato Sites and its Assets.
  2. Please take the time to read this policy carefully, and check it regularly as it may be amended from time to time. Your use of the Envato Sites is conditional on your acceptance of this policy.
  3. Any terms that are capitalized will have the meanings set out in the Definitions section of this policy. Words like ‘include’ and ‘including’ are not words of limitation.

So what's not acceptable use?

  1. It's NOT OKAY to use any Envato Site to upload, submit, post, build, create, host, distribute or otherwise make available any Content, that contains, provides access to (e.g. through links to third party websites) or promotes any of the following types of materials or activities:

a. Adult content: This includes material that is sexually explicit or pornographic (such as nudity or sexual activity) or promotes any commercial activity linked to adult content, such as escort agencies.

b. Exploitation of children: This includes material or activities that seek to harm or exploit children, threatens child safety, age-inappropriate material, or depicts children in a way that encourages or promotes child abuse, or attraction towards children.

c. Hate speech, terrorism and/or discrimination: This includes any form of speech, material or other activity that supports or condones violence or discrimination against individuals based on race, ethnicity, religion, disability, age, gender, nationality, sexual orientation or gender identity.

d. Incitement of harm or violence: This includes any material or activity that threatens, or that is intended to incite, promote or create violence or a risk of physical or mental harm, against an individual (including encouragement of self harm, or eating disorders), a group of individuals or promotes or encourages animal cruelty.

e. Harassment: This includes material or activity that involves any form of harassment, bullying, (including cyber-bullying), or threatening behavior against an individual or group of individuals.

f. Defamation: This includes material that contains any untruthful or defamatory material about a person that would have the likely tendency to lower their estimation in the eyes of others.

g. Infringement or violation of third party rights: Use of an Envato Site or Asset to share, create or distribute material in violation of the rights of others is not permitted, including infringement or likely infringement of intellectual property rights (including copyright and trade marks), location or property rights, or privacy rights (including any unauthorized impersonation of another person).

h. Offensive content: This includes material or activities that would cause offence to a reasonable person, including creating Content that is posted for ‘shock value' or is otherwise obscene, hateful or vulgar.

i. Fraudulent, misleading or deceptive conduct: This includes material or activities containing or involving any statements, information or disinformation that is false, misleading or deceptive.

j. Supply of regulated or illegal goods and services: This includes material or activities that promote the supply of weapons or gambling.

k. Illegal, unethical or criminal activities: This includes material or activities that violates or is likely to violate any applicable law or promotes activities that are illegal, unethical or criminal. 

l. Activities which cause harm to Envato or others: This includes material or activities which might cause harm to Envato, a Group Company or any other person. For example, pirated software, programs or archives that provide the functionality to gain unauthorised access to other systems or networks of any kind, Warez sites, files or web pages that contain viruses, trojans, malware or other applications designed to access a user's equipment or information with illegal intentions and/or without the knowledge of the user.

m. Unauthorized activities relating to artificial intelligence: This includes the use of Envato Sites or Assets  to train, develop, or enhance artificial intelligence models or machine learning algorithms, whether directly or indirectly. Any unauthorized use for such purposes will be considered a material breach of this policy and may result in immediate termination of access to Envato’s products and services and/or legal action.

n. Unauthorized activities that exploits sensitive subject matter: This includes material, that exploits, trivialises, or sensationalises sensitive or mature subject matter (such as domestic violence, sexual abuse or trauma) or in any other manner described under this section 4. 

To avoid doubt, if there are Assets available on an Envato Site that depict or reference sensitive topics, these Assets may only be used in a context where it serves an educational, informational, journalistic, or advocacy purpose. Misuse of an Asset under this section 4(n) may result in account suspension or immediate termination of access to Envato’s products and services and/or legal action.

  1. We reserve the right to take action under this policy if we identify that your Content includes material or promotes activities that are inconsistent with the spirit of this policy, even if it’s something that is not expressly forbidden under this policy. In other words, if you do something that isn’t listed here, but it looks or feels like something listed here, we may still take action.

Community participation

  1. Envato is founded on the idea of community and like any functioning and healthy community, some things are not allowed. It’s NOT OKAY to:

a. attempt to gain unauthorised access to computer systems, Assets through an Envato Site;

b. attempt to contact other members through an Envato Site or use any information gained from an Envato Site or an Asset with the intention to make a private arrangement that would otherwise be made using an Envato Site;

c. enter any arrangements that are not consistent with, or are intended to apply in addition to, the specific user terms and rules for using each of the Envato Sites or any Asset;

d. use information from an Envato Site or an Asset in a way that may confuse or mislead any third party (for example, gathering information to set up a site that looks like an Envato Site);

e. use or permit the use of any device, program or process to monitor, copy, or scrape all or any part of any Envato Site or Assets; and/or

f. attempt to or actually interrupt, negatively impact or alter any Envato Site in any way.

Investigation and reporting

  1. To protect our community, we use a combination of automated tools and human moderation to identify, review, and address Assets, Content or other User materials  that violate this policy and/or other applicable Envato terms, policies and guidelines.
  2. Our content moderators carefully review any potentially problematic Content or other User materials  that are flagged by our automated systems, as well as investigate reports we receive regarding unacceptable use. You agree to cooperate with us to investigate and remedy any violation of this policy.
  3. Users can report illegal Content via the “Reporting illegal content” form on our website. Reports about other unacceptable use, Assets,Content or other User materials can be made by emailing us at report.abuse@envato.com.  All reports will be addressed by our content moderators. We respond in the same way to any reports made by a government or public authority or law enforcement agency regarding a potential violation, but prioritise reports from those agencies which are classified under the Digital Services Act EU (DSA) as “trusted flaggers”, as required by law.

Enforcement and appeals

  1. We reserve the right to determine whether any use of an Envato Site, or use or creation of an Asset or any Content violates this policy at our sole discretion. Factors we may take into account when determining whether a violation of this policy has occurred, include:

    a. the absolute number or amount of unacceptable Assets, Content or other User materials uploaded or unfounded notices or complaints submitted;

    b. the relative proportion of the Asset, Content or other User materials or notices that are unacceptable;

    c. the gravity of the violation and its consequences;

    d. the intention of the recipient, individual, entity or complainant; and

    e. any previous violations of this policy.

  2. If we believe that your use of an Envato Site, or use or creation of any Assets, or any of your materials, Content or activities are in breach of this policy, we may immediately, without notice or liability and without affecting any other remedies available to us: 

    a. request that you remove, delete or disable the relevant Asset or other Content from the Envato Sites;

    b. remove, delete or disable the Assets or other Content, demote or restrict visibility of the Asset or Content or impose other measures relating to that Asset or other Content;

    c. suspend or terminate any accounts or agreements you have with Envato and/or your access to any of the Envato Sites, either permanently or temporarily;

    d. stop providing you with services, including hosting your website;

    e. in serious cases such as those involving the abuse of children, or other illegal activity, make a report to the appropriate authorities; and/or 

    f. any combination of any of the above actions.

  3. The suspension or termination of your access to an Envato Site or your Envato account may result in forfeiture of any licenses to Assets and other Content granted under the applicable Envato license terms, and termination of applicable memberships.
  4. We will respond to notices of alleged copyright infringement that comply with the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA). Information about our policy relating to claims of intellectual property infringement may be found here.
  5. The DSA gives European users of Envato Sites the right to challenge moderation decisions made by online platforms. If you don’t agree with a decision that we make under this policy you can submit an appeal within 180 days. You can appeal directly through our website or by lodging or responding to a Helpdesk ticket.
  6. If you’re not happy with the outcome of an appeal, you might be able to take things further through an out-of-court settlement or by going to court. The DSA requires EU Member States to approve out-of-court settlement bodies to handle disputes like these. Once certified, these bodies will be listed on a website managed by the European Commission. Decisions made by these out-of-court bodies aren’t binding on you or Envato.
  7. If you're not sure whether your Asset, Content, other materials or intended use of our services is acceptable, please contact us to discuss.

How can you contact us?

  1. If you have any questions about this policy, please contact us in writing at PO Box 16122 Collins Street West Victoria 8007 Australia or by email at report.abuse@envato.com.

Definitions

Assets: digital goods made available for license to a User of an Envato Site, including Items  created by Authors on Envato Elements and Envato Market (which includes but is not limited to any text, images, audio, code, video, templates, fonts and other proprietary materials), creative templates on Placeit, and AI-generated content created using any tool available on any Envato Site.

Author: a Member who creates and uploads Items to an Envato Site for licensing by Subscribers. 

Content: any information, prompt, post, data or other materials and content from a User of an Envato Site, that is: 

(a) built, created, uploaded, shared, or submitted to, or made available in connection with an Envato Site (including any Items provided by an Author, or User uploaded materials including prompts, or other text, images and other materials); or

(b) part of an End Product (whether as part of the Asset, or another component). 

End Product: the final work or product that is created that incorporates an Asset together with other components, so that it is larger in scope and different in nature than the original Asset.

Envato, we, us or our: Shutterstock, Inc.

Envato Sites: Envato Elements, Envato Market, Placeit, Mixkit, Envato Labs, Envato Tuts+, Reshot, Empowerkit and any other Envato platforms or sites which reference this policy, together with their associated websites, tools, products, services, Assets and other materials and content. 

Group Companies: Envato and any company that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with Envato.

Items: digital goods created by Authors and made available on Envato Elements and/or Envato Market, which may include goods like graphic design templates, fonts, WordPress themes, background music, After Effects project files and stock videos, graphics and photographs. 

Member: any User who creates and maintains an account with Envato and one of the Envato Sites, whether or not they are an Author or Subscriber.

Subscriber: a Member who purchases a subscription to an Envato Site.

User, you or your: each person who accesses or uses an Envato Site, whether or not they are an Author, Member or Subscriber.

results.name: Community Guidelines
results.title: Community Guidelines
results.body:
Envato brings together a global community of creatives - authors and customers alike - who may at times interact on our Envato Sites and platforms, including but not limited to on Envato Market (e.g. item comments and reviews) and on our official social media channels.

To keep these spaces safe, respectful, and professional, we ask all users to follow the rules below.

General Behaviour

Treat others with respect. Keep your interactions professional, constructive, and free from harassment, hate speech, or personal attacks. Criticism should focus on ideas or content, never on people. Offensive, discriminatory, or disruptive behaviour will not be tolerated.

Hard Rules

Please do not:

  • Discuss or attempt to influence the pricing of items or services governed by Author-Driven Pricing (on Envato Market). Strict rules preserve each author's right to independently set their prices. See this Help Center article on Setting Prices Responsibly for more details.
  • Engage in personal attacks, sabotage, or disruptive behaviour.
  • Post or promote content related to politics, pornography or religion or otherwise breach our Acceptable Use Policy.
  • Spam, excessively self-promote, or solicit donations or aid.
  • Link to free competing products, piracy, warez, or illegal activity of any kind.
  • Link directly to competitor sites or items (mentioning them by name in context is fine, but no links).
  • Request or share personal/identifying information about yourself or others.
  • Post anything that infringes on another person's intellectual property rights.
  • Also, everything on Envato Sites and social media channels should be considered PG rated or below. Please keep all communications, avatars, profile header images and videos clean.

Enforcement

Breaking these rules may result in removal of your posts, comments, or account access - with or without warning. Envato reserves the right to suspend, block, or terminate accounts at its discretion.

Legal notes

  • By using these spaces, you represent and warrant that your conduct complies with these rules, our Privacy Policy, our Acceptable Use Policy and all applicable laws, and that you will not infringe or misappropriate the rights of others.
  • Envato may update these rules from time to time, so please check back occasionally for the latest version.

Definitions

  • Envato, we, us or our: Shutterstock, Inc.
  • Envato Sites: Envato Elements, Envato Market, Placeit, Mixkit, Envato AI Tools, Envato Tuts+, Reshot, Empowerkit and any other Envato platforms or sites which reference these Community Rules, together with their associated websites and social media channels, tools, products, services, items and other Content.

results.name: Logo Templates Requirements
results.title: Logo Templates Requirements
results.body:
This article explains how Logo Templates need to be prepared and the technical requirements expected for this item type before you upload it to a Graphics category.

  • What is a Logo Template?
  • Technical Requirements
  • EPS Requirements
  • Tips for Designing Logo Templates

What is a Logo Template?

Logo Templates are distinct from custom, or bespoke logos. Logo Templates contain a graphic element plus editable text that can be modified by the user.

A Logo Template is a file that can be modified to have a custom name, tagline, and color scheme. The text is an integral part of the design, so the typography should work well with the overall concept and style. They are scalable and can be used for everything from business cards to billboards and printed documents to web designs.

Successful Logo Templates:

  • Are scalable
  • Have editable text.
  • Are legible large and small
  • Can be used for print and web
  • Are easy to customise by the end user

Technical Requirements

  • All files in the GraphicRiver Logo Templates category must be 100% vector
  • All Logo Templates must be in Illustrator EPS version 10 format.
  • The file must be CMYK.
  • Files, layers, and swatches must be organized and easy to use.
  • Text must be editable.
  • The item must include a help file to list the fonts used.
  • If you chose to use product mock-up for the main preview image, you must also include a plain version of the design, so customers can see the logo clearly. 
  • Layers and objects should not be locked.
  • There should be no visible guides.
  • The file must be constructed well.
  • Graphic elements should be made with the minimum number of points possible to define the shapes, this ensures that the paths are smooth. Excessive points can make the file difficult to edit and can show irregularities at higher magnifications. 

EPS Requirements

Before submitting your logo template, ensure that your file meets the following EPS requirements:

  • The EPS file must be version 10 compatible.
  • There should be no stray points. Stray points are invisible points that have no stroke or fill and cannot be seen without closely inspecting your design.
  • Stray points can occur when lines are cut and deleted or the Pen Tool has been used on the artboard without drawing a path. You can find stray points in a few different ways, one is by looking at your design in outline mode. In Adobe Illustrator, you can go to Select - Object - Stray Points. 
  • There should be no open paths. All filled paths must be closed or they can cause problems when the file is edited and customized. For more information, read Dealing with Open Paths article. 
  • Layers and objects should not be hidden or locked.
  • The file cannot contain rasterized elements or un-expanded effects. Logo Templates must be 100% editable vectors and cannot contain rasterized elements. To find rasterized content in an Illustrator EPS file, you can open the Links Panel, go to Window - Links. 

Once you have your Logo Template file ready to sell, you should follow our guide to preparing your item for upload.

Tips for Designing Logo Templates

  • Avoid designs that convey a specific concept, general designs will appeal to a greater number of subscribers.
    • However, designs should not be so generic as to be meaningless.
    • For example, using a set of letters or words as a graphic element will limit the number of names that can be used when customizing the template.
  • Graphic elements that represent a specific concept can also prove challenging when adding a custom name. If a graphic element relies on the accompanying text to give the design context, it will not be suitable as a Logo Template.

  • Before you begin your design, think about the concept and the ease of customization. 
    It may be helpful to trial your logo template with a variety of names before you upload it for review.
  • The logo must have a graphic element and a name (tagline is optional).
  • The logo must have editable text.
  • The logo must be suitable for all sizes - from business cards to billboards.

Please note that it is important to refine and optimize the elements in your design. Fine details and text won’t print well at small scales. Errors and inconsistencies in your design will stand out when the logo is enlarged.

  • The text and graphic element must be balanced:
  • The visual balance of the logo should be aesthetically pleasing. Each element needs to work together to create a unified design.
  • Poor alignment or scaling of the graphic element and text can cause the logo template to look unbalanced.
  • The choice of the font must compliment the graphic element so that the logo appears to be a single coherent design.
  • Non-standard fonts must include a link to the font used in both the item description and a help file. Read our full article on using outside assets for more information.
  • Layers, swatches, and colour pallets should be well organised. Keep the layers unlocked. If possible, separate the elements into different layers.
  • Make sure the file is easy to customise. Subscribers appreciate files that are quick and easy to use.

Important: When you use a font and link to it in the item description and help file, be sure to choose a legal, reputable font site. System fonts do not need a link.

Graphic elements that represent a specific concept can prove to be challenging when adding a custom name. If a graphic element relies on the accompanying text to give the design context, it will not be suitable as a Logo Template.


 

 

The logo template must have a graphic element and a name (tagline is optional).


Important: Logos that are created using text only may not provide enough value for the subscriber and could be removed from the library.

Logo creation kits are useful when the design relies on a specific combination of letters. The file has a larger audience and the subscribers can select a letter combination that matches their needs.


 
Design Credit: Vintage Monogram Logo Kit, By Sztufi

Important: Monograms must be your own creation or made with assets you own the appropriate license for. Refer to clause 24 d & e of the Elements Author Agreement. 

Uploading lots of individual monogram logos that are part of the same design family could breach the Elements library rules. This may result in items being removed from the library.

Layer Styles (.ai) and Appearances (.psd) allow the user to keep the look and feel of the design. We recommended that you include a help file if your design takes advantage of these features. 

Design Credit: Dwarf Esports Logo by Suhandi

results.name: Vectors Category Requirements
results.title: Vectors Category Requirements
results.body:
Summary: This article explains how Vectors need to be prepared and the technical requirements expected for this item type.

Table of Contents

  • Technical Requirements
  • Optional Files
  • Examples

Technical Requirements

  • Illustrator **EPS 10 compatible**.
  • Can be either RGB or CMYK.
  • Making it easy for customers to modify.
  • Must be 100% vector - no raster elements or effects.
  • No open paths unless they are unfilled (i.e., strokes with no fill).
  • No locked objects.
  • No hidden objects.
  • Clean and well organized (remove stray shapes, empty layers, etc.).
  • Layers should be unlocked.
  • Groups, if used, should be logical.
  • Custom fills and brush strokes should be expanded.

Optional Files

You are welcome to include additional files and file types, such as AI and JPEG. For example, you may want to provide a JPEG for users who cannot edit the vector file.

You may wish to include an AI file with unexpanded brush strokes and effects. These extra files should be listed in the item description and item details. Any special instructions can be noted in a help file included in the download folder.

Examples

Example 1: Must be 100% vector - no raster elements or effects.

Example 2: No open paths unless they are unfilled (i.e., strokes with no fill).

Example 3: Layers should not be locked.

Example 4: No stray shapes outside the Artboard.

Example 5: Custom brush strokes should be expanded. Unexpanded brush stroke (top), and expanded brush stroke (bottom).

Example 6: Custom fills should be expanded. Unexpanded pattern fill (left), and expanded pattern fill (right).

results.name: The DMCA Process
results.title: The DMCA Process
results.body:
If you believe your intellectual property rights have been infringed, this article will help you submit a DMCA Takedown Notice or a General IPR Notice to us, for the content to be removed from Envato’s sites.

If you are an author who has received a DMCA Takedown Notice and your item has been removed, this article will help you understand the options open to you and includes information on submitting a Counter Notice.

How to submit a valid DMCA Takedown Notice

If you believe someone is using your copyright content without permission, you can use the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) process by sending us a DMCA takedown notice. As the service provider of the Envato platforms, we act promptly when we receive valid DMCA takedown notices.

Please make sure you understand what rights you are claiming before you submit a DMCA takedown notice because it is a serious legal document. Consider whether you need legal advice. It's really important not to make false claims as this could have serious legal consequences.

If the DMCA takedown notice is not in a valid format we will ask you to resubmit with the missing information.

For us to action a DMCA takedown notice, it must be in a valid format, which means it must include the information set out at points 1-5 below.

  1. Explain the content of the Author’s item that you claim infringes your copyright, including a description and where we can find it the Author’s item - include the URL;
  2. Explain your copyrighted content and let us know where we can see this published - include the URL;
  3. Give us a detailed explanation about how you believe the content in the Author’s item violates your copyright;
  4. Include your full name and contact details, including your address, phone number, and email address;
  5. Include the following two statements:
    • "I have a good faith belief that use of the copyrighted materials described above as allegedly infringing is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law." AND
    • "I swear, under penalty of perjury, that the information in the notification is accurate and that I am the copyright owner or am authorized to act on behalf of the owner of an exclusive right that is allegedly infringed."
  6. By law, you need to sign and date your DMCA take down notice either with a physical or digital signature. If you want to sign a physical document you'll need to scan the document and attach it to the help ticket.

We have to send this DMCA takedown notice to the other person, which means your details will be passed to them. The other person, who is the Author of the item you have identified, can submit a DMCA counter-notification if they disagree with your DMCA takedown notice, and they might contact you directly using your contact details.

The content in the Author’s item in question will generally be disabled from Envato when we receive a DMCA takedown notice. If we receive a counter-notification and you have not confirmed to us that you've filed court proceedings against the Author within 10 business days, we will re-enable the content within 14 business days of receiving the counter-notification. If you have any further questions please visit our DMCA FAQ page.

What to consider if you have received a DMCA Takedown Notice

If you receive a DMCA takedown notice, you can consider whether you think the claims made in the notice are valid. You might choose to seek legal advice, especially if you're not sure whether there is any legal validity to the claim.

  • You can choose to accept a DMCA takedown notice - if so your content will remain disabled.
  • Or, you can choose to respond to a DMCA takedown notice by sending us a DMCA counter-notification.

How to submit a Counter Notice

Please take care to understand this process because it is possible that the claimant can take legal action against you if you file a counter-notification. If you have any further questions please visit our DMCA FAQ page.

It's really important not to make a false claim, as this could have serious legal consequences. Please seek your own advice if you're not sure about what the counter-notification process means.

If the DMCA counter notification is not in a valid format we will ask you to resubmit with the missing information.

For us to action a DMCA counter notification it must be in a valid format, which means it must include the information set out in the points below. There is an example template for your reference:

  1. Explain the content in your item that has been taken down, including a description and where it was found - include the URL (this is on the original DMCA notice).
  2. Provide an explanation for your Counter Notice
  3. Make a formal statement about why you think the content in your item should be reinstated. Include the following words: “I make this statement under penalty of perjury, I have a good faith belief that the content was...[add the reason why the content was not used in an unauthorized way]” (for example “removed or disabled as a result of mistake or misidentification of the content”.
  4. Include your full name and contact details, including your address, phone number, and email address.
  5. If you are a US resident, include a statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of Federal District Court for the judicial district where you live.
  6. If you live outside the United States, include a statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of the courts in Victoria, Australia (where Envato is based), and the courts located in the United States federal district in which the person who sent the DMCA takedown notice (claimant) lives.
  7. Include a statement that you will accept service of process from the claimant or their agent.

By law, you need to sign and date your notice either with a digital or physical signature. If you send us the information via Envato Support, please state SIGNED followed by your full name. If you want to sign a physical document you'll need to scan the document and attach it to the help ticket.

We'll send a copy of the DMCA counter-notification to the person who sent the DMCA takedown notice (claimant), then wait 10 business days. Unless the claimant sends us a notice that court proceedings have been filed against you within the 10 business days, we'll then reinstate the content within 14 business days from when we received the counter-notification.

How to submit a General IPR Notice

As the DMCA process only applies to copyright, we have a similar process for other claims (General IPR Notices). If you believe that an Author’s item on Envato Elements is using content that is protected by another form of IPR (not copyright), such as a trademark, we ask you to send us a General IPR Notice that contains the detailed information set out below. We’ve set out an example template which you can use, see GENERAL IPR NOTICE TEMPLATE.

  1. Tell us about the content in the Author’s item that you claim infringes your rights, including a description and where we can find it - include the URL;
  2. Tell us about the rights you claim, the basis of the ownership claim, and where we can see evidence of your right - include the URL. If you're claiming a trademark right include the trademark registration number, country and class of registration;
  3. Give us a detailed explanation about how you believe the content in the Author’s item violates your claimed right; and
  4. Include your full name and contact details, including address, phone number and email address. You need to sign and date your notice. If you send us the information via Envato Author Help please note that by entering your full name you are providing us with your digital signature which is legally binding. If you want to sign a physical document you'll need to scan the document and attach it to the help ticket.

We will respond appropriately depending on what your claim is about. We may ask for more information and send a copy of your claim to the Author. The Author might contact you directly using the details you've provided.

What to consider if you have received a General IPR Notice or another type of complaint

Complaints about the use of IPRs can cover a wide range of issues. If we send you a general IPR notice or tell you that another type of complaint has been made, we'll generally ask you some specific questions about the complaint and the content or let you know what else is needed.

results.title: Add-ons Requirements
results.body:
Summary: This article explains how Add-on items need to be prepared and the technical requirements expected for this item type. 

Table of Contents

  • File Preparation
  • Documentation Requirements
  • Technical Requirements for Photoshop
  • Technical Requirements for Adobe Illustrator

File Preparation

Follow the below file preparation guidelines:

  • Use a concise name for your file, this will assist customers once they have downloaded the item.
  • Organise the contents of the file so that it is easy to use and make sure that your help file is easy to locate.
  • Name your groups and layers in English. The following screenshot shows a well-organized action set, you can see how each action is clearly labelled:


    Following is an example of organized file:
  • Make sure to fill out the Works With section, including
    • The colorspace of your document (at the minimum, an RGB file should be included)
    • The version of Adobe programs the item is designed to work with.
  • Files should be fully compatible with English language Adobe Software versions.
  • Always favour non-destructive techniques such as Smart Objects and Layer Styles. 

Documentation Requirements

As part of the documentation guidelines, ensure that you include:

  • All your files are included.
  • An installation walkthrough.
  • Required general instructions notes.
  • Input options and modifiers.
  • Details of fonts used.
  • Common issues/bugs that might arise for the customer and how to resolve them (particularly with actions).

Technical Requirements for Photoshop Add-ons

Actions

  • Required File Format: .ATN
    Optional File: .PSD
  • You must include assets referenced in your action, such as any PAT, ASL or ABR files.

    Actions should not produce errors.
  • In your documentation, you should guide the customer through any typical customization and modifier input panes.
  • Note that actions produced in non-English Adobe software programs may be incompatible with native English installations. The marketplace requires full support for English systems.

Brushes

  • Required File Format: .ABR

A high-resolution mask, 2500 pixels square.

Text Styles

  • Required File Format: .ASL
  • Optional PSD - Complex and detailed styles can require multiple layers, in this case, the inclusion of a PSD file may be necessary.
  • Be sure to include information in your help file that explains how to transfer complex Multi-Layer Styles to other Photoshop documents.
  • Layer Styles may make use of smart objects, but make sure that a Layer Style is easy to move to another file and retains as much flexibility as possible.
  • Any Patterns used within the styles must be included as a PAT file
  • Patterns require seamless repetition.

Photoshop Shapes

  • Required File Format: .CSH
  • Shapes cannot be clipped or have distorted perspective.
  • Curves and paths must be smooth and uniform unless it’s appropriate to the design to have a stylised edge (for example, grunge or low poly shapes).

                             Rough, non-uniform curves and jagged edges.

Photoshop Patterns

  • Required File Format: .PAT
  • Patterns must be seamless and tileable
  • Patterns must repeat seamlessly in both the X and Y axis

An error in this repeating pattern.

Technical Requirements for Adobe Illustrator

Actions

  • Required File Format: .AIA
  • Your action  must work exactly as is demonstrated in the preview image
  • You must upload detailed instructions on how to install, use and customize your action file, including any input panes and variables.
  • Note that actions produced with non-English versions of Adobe software may be incompatible with native English versions. GraphicRiver requires full support for English language systems.

Graphic Styles

  • Required File Format: .AI
  • Files must be 100% vector.

Brushes

  • You cannot include raster elements in your file. 
  • Before you upload a brush set to GraphicRiver, test how it works around tight oblique corners and overlapping paths. Some designs may not work well, in this case, and your file may not be approved.

results.body:
Summary: This article explains how animated graphics need to be prepared and the technical requirements expected for this item type.

Table of Contents

  • General requirements
  • File requirements

General requirements

  • Files must demonstrate mastery of technical elements (line quality, color usage, composition, graphics styles and trends) and application of design principles and animation.
  • The animation should feature seamless looping and smooth, fluid motion.
  • Animations must be relevant to the illustration.
  • Animations cannot be based on other Authors’ illustrations; you (the submitting Author) must be both the illustrator and the animator.

File Requirements

  • All submissions must be a JSON Lottie file. The system will automatically provide derivative files in MP4, GIF, SVG, and PNG.
  • The minimal loop length is 2 seconds and the loop must be seamless.
